items.title: Draft: feat(minder): offer glab minder setup after commands in governed projects
items.body:
## Description

After a successful glab command, glab now offers to run `glab minder setup` when it matters:

- the repository's origin is a GitLab project on a host glab is logged in to
- AI Governance is on for that project
- Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode has run on this machine
- setup has not been run

Only a person at an interactive terminal is asked, with standard output on the terminal too, outside CI and with prompts turned on. glab never asks on Windows, after help, after `glab minder` commands, agent hooks, commands that serve until stopped, or the commands the update check and telemetry skip.

The prompt is shown on standard error, names the agents it found, and offers Yes, Not now and Never. Yes starts `glab minder setup` for those agents in a new glab process, which shows its usual consent prompt before it installs anything. Not now asks again in 7 days, and so does uninstalling. Never sets the new `no_minder_prompt` setting in the global configuration, and `GLAB_NO_MINDER_PROMPT` turns the prompt off too.

When glab detects a coding agent instead, it prints one line a day for each project, asking the agent to have the user run setup in their own terminal.

To check whether AI Governance is on, glab makes one request that lists the project's agent sessions, which changes nothing on GitLab, with a 2 second limit. It keeps an answer for a day for each project and retries after an hour when GitLab does not answer. glab saves the cache and the answer before it acts, so when it cannot save them it neither calls GitLab nor asks. Any failure means glab does not ask.

The update check now also skips `glab auth git-credential` and `glab auth credential-helper`, which it missed because it only looked at the first argument.

It is stacked on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4531, which stops coding agents from running setup.

Related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/641757

## How has this been tested?

Table-driven tests use a fake GitLab server that only accepts the sessions request for the encoded project path, a mocked Git remote and an isolated configuration. They cover every gate:

- CI, no terminal, standard output piped, prompts turned off and Windows
- outside a Git repository, or on a host glab is not logged in to
- governance off, a missing licence and an API error
- no agent installed, or setup already done
- the 7-day snooze, Never and the environment variable
- a cache or answer that cannot be saved

Terminal tests answer each choice. They check that the prompt names the agents found and that Yes sets up only those agents, and they cover a setup that cannot start. The Yes test runs the real setup command to show that its consent prompt appears and that declining it installs nothing.

Other tests cover keeping an answer for a day and no answer for an hour, including an unreachable host and a cache file that holds `null`. They also cover the agent line, printed once a day and never after help, `glab minder`, `glab govern` or serve commands, that the command's output is unchanged and prompts go to standard error, the `glab minder setup` command line and streams, the skip check for commands that shells and Git run, the sessions request in `gaig`, and the snooze after uninstall.

The govern, `cmd/glab`, api and config tests pass, lint is clean on Linux and macOS, and comment-overlap is clean.

items.title: fix(minder): refuse setup and uninstall from coding agents
items.body:
## Description

A coding agent could run `glab minder setup --yes` or `glab minder setup --uninstall --yes` and confirm setup or uninstall for the user. Uninstall matters too, because removing the hooks stops the audit trail. When glab detects a coding agent from an explicit agent signal, setup and uninstall now refuse to run, with or without `--yes` and with or without a terminal. The error names the agent and asks the user to run the command in their own terminal. An `AI_AGENT` of `1`, `true` or `yes` counts as an unnamed agent.

IDE terminals detected only from `TERM_PROGRAM`, such as Cursor's, are not refused, because a person may be typing there. The new `DetectRunningAgent`, stored in `BuildInfo.RunningAgent`, makes that distinction from where the signal came from rather than from the agent's name. Detection reads the environment variables agents set, so an agent that sets none is not detected. The setup help and the governance rules say so.

Related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/641757

## How has this been tested?

A new table-driven test runs the setup command through `cmdtest`. It covers setup and uninstall from an agent with `--yes`, without `--yes`, with a terminal and without one, and from an unnamed agent. It also covers runs with no agent and in IDE terminals. The uninstall cases start with the hooks installed and check that a refused uninstall leaves them in place. Another table-driven test covers `DetectRunningAgent`, including IDE terminals, Zed's agent terminal and the `AI_AGENT` values.

The govern, `cmd/glab` and api tests pass, lint is clean on Linux and macOS, and comment-overlap is clean.
